strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine benchmark headroom erosion with timely relevance
Rigorous 4-part curation pipeline with quality controls (peer review of questions, iterative refinement)
Comprehensive evaluation of 20 diverse models with multiple metrics (pass@1, pass@5, k/k reliability) and excellent reproducibility (full hyperparameters, model versions, canary string)
Practical lightweight design (100 questions) enabling evaluation of expensive reasoning models (~$0.5/question for o1)
Valuable error analysis finding that visual interpretation errors dominate over reasoning errors, contrasting with prior benchmarks
High-quality qualitative failure cases demonstrating recurring systematic issues (counting, spatial reasoning, fine-grained detail)
weaknesses: Circular benchmark design: adversarial filtering that removes all correctly-answered questions guarantees 0% performance by construction, making results inevitable rather than discovered; undermines 'impossible' framing and future model scoring

Lack of systematic question categorization explicitly acknowledged by authors ('not feasible to assign distinct categories'), preventing diagnostic analysis of which visual skills improve and limiting scientific insight

Questionable value proposition: reasoning models (o1 using 7.3k tokens vs. standard models using hundreds) show no performance advantage despite motivation for test-time scaling, adequately unexplained
Limited methodological novelty: standard manual curation plus adversarial filtering approach; primary contribution is the specific question set rather than novel methods or frameworks
Insufficient differentiation from existing hard benchmarks: VibeEval has 50% unanswerable questions, HLE achieves ~10% performance; limited justification for why ZeroBench's 0% approach is superior

Evaluation methodology concerns: exact string matching without clear precision requirements for numerical answers; dismissal of partial credit lacks rigor; inconsistent multi-image handling (separate vs. collage formats)
Image resolution acknowledged as potential bottleneck preventing progress but not systematically explored; different models may receive different resolutions through various APIs
Error analysis lacks rigor: visual vs. reasoning error categorization based on manual inspection without systematic sampling, inter-rater agreement, or statistical quantification
Benchmark shelf-life concerns: authors acknowledge 'impossible' status won't persist long; unlike ARC-AGI, no principled approach ensures sustained relevance beyond near-term model development
Subquestions show substantial signal (12-24% pass@1 vs. 0% main questions) but lack categorization and analysis of what this gap indicates about benchmark properties

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly articulated observation that benchmarks lose headroom rapidly as models improve, with concrete evidence presented
Rigorous curation pipeline: Four-stage process (feedback, initial evaluation, review, adversarial filtering) is thorough and uses multiple frontier models for quality control
Comprehensive evaluation: 20 diverse models evaluated including reasoning models (o1, QVQ), with multiple metrics (pass@1, pass@5, k/k reliability) and token cost analysis
Excellent presentation: Clear writing, well-organized, comprehensive appendix with exact prompts, hyperparameters, model versions enabling reproducibility
Extensive qualitative analysis: Figures 7-13 provide illustrative failure cases across multiple error categories (counting, spatial reasoning, fine-grained detail)
High-quality manual curation: Diverse questions covering both natural and synthetic images, single and multi-image settings, multiple domains
weaknesses: Adversarial filtering as a fundamental design flaw: By filtering to achieve exactly 0% pass@1, the benchmark becomes brittle and less informative. The 0% result is a design artifact rather than an empirical finding. Authors acknowledge 'reasonable likelihood of low non-zero scores when evaluating new models...even if their capabilities are not superior,' undermining the ability to measure progress

Limited novelty and insight: Main contribution is 100 hard visual questions—useful but incremental. Error analysis confirms existing findings (SPACE, BLINK, prior work) that visual interpretation dominates bottlenecks without offering new understanding of causes or solutions

Small scale and statistical concerns: 100 questions is quite small; pass@5 results show only 1-7 correct answers with high variance, making it difficult to form reliable hierarchies or draw conclusions. Adversarial filtering further limits interpretability

Benchmark longevity questionable: Despite title promising relevance over time, authors expect ZeroBench to become solvable soon. Unlike ARC-AGI (hard for 5+ years), adversarial filtering against current models doesn't guarantee calibration for future capabilities

Evaluation inconsistencies: o1 pro and QVQ use different parsing method (Gemini 2 Flash) vs. automatic regex parsing; multi-image questions handled differently across models (separate vs. collage)—potential fairness and comparability concerns

Unclear practical utility: Pass@5 scores show all models scoring 0% on main questions even with multiple attempts. No analysis of which visual capabilities are hardest, no correlation with model properties, no actionable insights for model developers

Missing deeper investigation: No categorization of questions by type/difficulty; no analysis of why reasoning models show no advantage despite longer chains; no sensitivity analysis on adversarial filtering threshold; limited mechanistic insight

Limited analysis of surprising findings: Reasoning models generate 3-7x more tokens but show no performance advantage—mentioned but not explored. This could have motivated deeper investigation into bottlenecks
Potential creator bias: 20+ creators with 'deliberately broad' instructions; no inter-annotator agreement analysis or diversity metrics; potential consensus bias in what constitutes 'impossible'

strengths: Addresses well-documented and urgent problem of benchmark saturation with clear motivation (Figures 1-2)
Rigorous 4-part curation pipeline with adversarial filtering, cross-review, and quality control demonstrates excellent benchmark design practice
Comprehensive evaluation of 20 diverse models (proprietary, open-source, reasoning-focused) with multiple evaluation modalities (pass@1, pass@k, k/k reliability)
Excellent reproducibility: complete hyperparameters, model versions, prompts, and public release commitment enable future verification
Practical design choices (100 questions, lightweight format) explicitly motivated by computational costs of reasoning models with test-time scaling
Transparent discussion of limitations including transient nature of benchmark, image resolution constraints, and difficulty of creating 'impossible' questions
Detailed error analysis with extensive failure case examples (Appendix E) showing consistent patterns across all models
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: straightforward approach (create hard questions, filter via adversarial removal) with precedent in prior work (VibeEval, HLE)
Inherent selection bias from adversarial filtering creates artificial performance floor; unclear whether 0% reflects impossibility or efficient removal of solvable questions
Many failures attributed to image resolution constraints rather than reasoning limitations, somewhat undermining 'impossible' framing and suggesting architectural rather than conceptual barriers
Error analysis primarily qualitative with selective examples (Figures 7-13) rather than quantitative breakdown; lacks systematic categorization of failure types across all questions
Missing inter-annotator agreement metrics despite 20+ question creators and claims of 'high-quality and noise-free' labels; no documented quality validation
Limited insight into root causes: documents that models fail at counting/spatial reasoning (confirming known issues) but doesn't explain why or propose solutions
Small benchmark scale (100 questions) limits statistical power and category breakdown; pass@5 scores are extremely small (1-7 correct per model), raising variance concerns
Transient benchmark: title explicitly acknowledges it won't remain 'impossible' for long, limiting long-term research value
Reasoning model analysis (Table 3, Section 5.2) shows o1/QVQ use 7.3k tokens with zero performance advantage but lacks deeper interpretation of this surprising finding
